chunks: If they had believed in God and the Prophet and what had been revealed to him, they would never have held them as allies; and many among them are transgressors.
ai.seo_question: Why did the People of the Book take each other as allies according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the disconnect between nominal belief and political loyalty, noting that the People of the Book formed alliances (like the Banu Qurayza) against Muslims despite acknowledging Muhammad’s prophethood. The term 'fasiqun' (transgressors) is interpreted not merely as sinners but as those who deviate from the covenant of faith by prioritizing tribal or communal interests over divine unity. This underscores the Shia emphasis on 'Wilayah' (spiritual and political guardianship) as the true marker of sincere belief.
